focus: Audit Gate-3 injection end-to-end across all six runtimes
noveltyJustification: Seven findings were fully new and one partially refined prior payload and delivery measurements: (7 + 0.5) / 8 = 0.9375, rounded to 0.94.
keyQuestions: How does Gate 3 classify, persist, inject, deduplicate, and enforce across six runtimes?
What is the actual positive/negative payload cost and where can repetition be safely conditionalized?
answeredQuestions: Established source-level classifier/state behavior, six-runtime transport differences, terminal versus open-epoch repetition, and exact fixed positive/negative cost.
ruledOut: Cursor configured cost is observed cost
OpenCode repeated-transform duplication is already live-observed
sourcesQueried: runtime registration files and process-test anchors
local compiled-classifier and fixed-string measurement output

summary: Satisfied/skipped states deduplicate terminally, but every positive prompt in an unresolved open epoch re-emits 521 bytes.
Cursor relies on session prebind because prompt delivery is inactive; OpenCode may reclassify one fetched user message across multiple transforms.
Classifier comments and framework exemption/menu prose diverge from executable behavior and current routing nuance.
Read-only and terminal states are zero-cost; repetition is limited to unresolved positive or invalid-answer cases.
